text:
jordan: heads up — noticed a ~15% drop in kv/prefix cache hit-rate for the /generate route since ~02:00 UTC. graph looks spiky. who owns the alert and where's the best dashboard to look? :eyes:

maria: grafana panel here: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/prefix-cache?orgId=1&var-route=generate — check the `prefix_cache_hitrate` and `prefix_cache_evictions` panels. alert name is `kv_prefix_hitrate_low`.

samir: devops-bot just fired on that alert at 1765599950 — pinging oncall. quick check: is this customer-visible latency or just background miss noise?

devops-bot: Alert: kv_prefix_hitrate_low (fired)
  - route: /generate
  - current: 0.58
  - threshold: 0.65
  - window: 5m
  - alert link: https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/kv_prefix_hitrate_low/1765599950

alisa: quick triage checklist: 1) confirm metric source (prometheus vs runtime export), 2) look at eviction spikes, 3) check recent rollouts to runtime or model. I saw a minor runtime release at 01:45 — tagging henry to confirm.

henry: I rolled out a small change to the kv cache eviction pacing at 01:40 to reduce memory pressure. It changed the eviction backoff algo; I noted decreased memory but didn't expect hit-rate impact. will rollback if this is correlated.

jordan: ok can someone paste the prometheus query you usually use? i want to grab a 24h comparison.

maria: use this promql for 5m avg: `avg_over_time(prefix_cache_hitrate{route="/generate"}[5m])` and for evictions: `increase(prefix_cache_evictions_total{route="/generate"}[5m])`. for 24h: change [5m] to [24h] on rate funcs or use `avg_over_time(...[24h])`.

samir: to repro locally (cheap): send a burst of short prompts to /generate with same prefixes to simulate cold keys. example: `for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/generate -d '{"prompt":"test $i","max_tokens":1}' & done` — watch prefix hit-rate drop then recover.

alisa: Loki query for logs around evictions: `{job="runtime"} |= "prefix eviction" | json` then filter `|= "route=/generate"`. look for `evicted_keys` field spikes.

jordan: thanks. if the rollout caused it, what's our plan? temporary rollback or tune alert to reduce noise while we investigate?

henry: i'll roll back the eviction pacing change in canary now and post the deploy id. if hit-rate recovers, we need a follow-up to adjust backoff parameters and run perf tests.

maria: regarding alert tuning — current window is 5m and threshold 0.65. we get a lot of transient dips during traffic bursts. propose: change to window 10m and threshold 0.60, and add a `for: 10m` in the alert rule to avoid chattiness. file a PR to infra-alerts and tag eng-platform and oncall.

samir: sounds reasonable. can we add a dashboard panel annotating deploys so it's easier to correlate in future?

alisa: yes — I can add a small annotation panel and a link to the rollback runbook. also suggest adding a synthetic probe that hits a few representative prefixes every 2m so we get earlier signal for regressions.

jordan: assigning follow-ups: henry to rollback and confirm, maria to open infra-alerts PR with proposed new window/threshold, alisa to add deploy annotation and probe plan. i'll update the incident thread if any customer impact shows. :thumbsup:

henry: rollback applied to canary: deploy id `deploy-20231115-evict-rollback`, timestamp 1765600200. monitoring now.

maria: opened PR https://git.redwood.example/infra-alerts/pulls/212 — proposed `for: 10m`, threshold 0.60. cc @eng-platform.

samir: monitoring grafana, hit-rate already trending back up to ~0.7. will watch for 30m and then close out.

jordan: awesome, thanks everyone. will follow up with a short postmortem summary once we have the final numbers.

(END)
